advice: Abstain. No distinct legal fusion is established from the supplied evidence. A 16×16 transpose tile computed separately for each 32-column B panel would repeat work across 16 panels: 16 MiB of A reads and 16 MiB of transposed values produced, versus one 1 MiB full A transpose. Reusing those tiles across panels would need additional buffering or a changed traversal; neither has been specified and checked here. The prior TB measurements test whole-call wrappers and do not isolate transpose cost.
risks: The previous NEON-transpose TB candidate was rejected after 10 reports: it won 2/10 pairs, scored 600.02–962.86 GFLOP/s against controls at 800.80–1093.42, and did not pass the promotion gate. That outcome does not establish transpose as the cause. Any future fusion proposal needs exact tile and ZA mapping, repeated-work and data-movement counts, and checks for FP32 K-order, full C overwrite, fresh inputs, general sizes, tails, n≤0, and allocation failure. If measured, retain the ten-report and paired-control rules, historical and fresh peak comparisons, and held-out gate.
